text.p: French first division matches on Wednesday (standings in brackets, all 1900 gmt kick-off):

Leaders PSG will be wary of taking Lille, surprise fourth, lightly despite beating them 4-0 in pre-season friendly in August and bearing in mind their home defeat by same side last season. PSG defender Benoit Cauet is out with injury.

Monaco, looking to bounce back from defeat at Marseille last week, have bulging sick bay with Enzo Scifo, Marco Grassi, Eric Di Meco, Emmanuel Petit and Philippe Leonard all injured. Strasbourg striker Pascal Nouma, who scored both goals in 2-1 win over Montpellier last week, is suspended and goalkeeper Alexander Vencel on international duty with Slovakia.

In-form UEFA Cup contenders Metz, fresh from surprise come-from-behind 3-2 win away to champions Auxerre last week, should prove too strong for Rennes, whose chief weapon is first division's 12-goal top scorer Stephane Guivarc'h.

Slovenian international striker Ermin Siljak's transfer has finally been completed after nearly five months of problems and he is available to line up in attack alongside Yugoslav Anton Drobnjak, a bonus for Bastia in view of long-term absence of Slovakian broken break victim Lubomir Moravcik.

Daniel Sanchez praised his injury-hit Nice side -- worst defence with 30 goals against in 16 matches -- for their fighting spirit in 1-0 defeat by leaders PSG last week and is confident good result will turn their fortunes.
Lens have goalkeeper Jean-Claude Nadon and defender Eric Sikora back from injury, while Bordeaux will be without striker Didier Tholot and defender Patrick Colleter, both suspended.

Local police are treating Marseille visit as high risk and taking appropriate security measures. Marseille, whose captain Jean-Philippe Durand is doubtful with sore knee, will be looking to confirm they have turned corner after fine 3-1 home win over Monaco. Cannes have worst attack with 10 goals, only five at home, in 16 matches.

The champions will be looking for quick recovery from shock of conceding two goals in last five minutes of shock 3-2 defeat at home to Metz last week. Midfielder Antoine Sibierski is still unavailable through injury, while Guingamp welcome back goalkeeper Angelo Hugues from injury.
Montpellier have Ivory Coast striker Ibrahim Bakayoko and libero William Prunier suspended, while Caen have full squad as they attempt to pull further away from bottom.
